scope_gaps.note: The advice generalises from one condition of Study 4 (about 1 hour of work on a computer tutorial assignment, psychology undergraduates, 1 or 2 week deadlines) to any new task and any person. The tested procedure was structured (list past assignments, state how far before the deadline they were typically finished, compute a date on that basis, write a scenario from past experience) and 'porównaj' is looser. In the General Discussion the authors say they have no compelling evidence that recollection of past performance improves the accuracy of time estimates; the item does not claim accuracy.
The source asked about the distribution of several earlier assignments relative to their deadlines and a typical finish time, not the duration of the one previous similar task.
Same population and task limits as the title; the tested procedure had two extra questions and a written scenario, which the item mentions only as 'zapisz, jak ... odnoszą się'.

Participants were instructed and prompted by two specific questions to link past and present, not merely free to compare. The source reports that even then only 12.5% of this group mentioned past experience in their thought listing. The item does not say how the linking was done.
Group sizes were 41 (control) and 40 (recall-relevant) per the Table 4 note; a third group (recall only, 38.1%) is not mentioned in the sentence, which compares only the two named groups.

The figure is the difference in the share of participants who finished within their own predicted time. It is not a difference in speed or in accuracy; the source reports no difference in actual completion times or absolute error.
'Nie uniwersalny' is weaker than the source: in this experiment there was no productivity change at all (actual completion times were equal across conditions).
'Studentów' were undergraduate psychology students who took part for course credit; the word is not wrong but the population is narrower than students in general.
'Krótkie' refers to about 1 hour of work; the predicted and actual completion times covered days (actual means from 4.3 to 9.1 days across deadline conditions) because subjects had 1 or 2 weeks.

The source reports no significant effect of thought focus on absolute error and on actual completion time, which is not proof of no difference; the item states it as 'nie przyspieszyła ... nie zmniejszyła'.

The two lead snapshots (2757a11eba265541.txt, 4cec846a0874c64c.txt) were not opened because leads are not evidence. Nothing outside the allowed set was opened; no protocol violation. The full-text snapshot is a two-column PDF extraction: columns are interleaved line by line and there are OCR artefacts (joined words, a few garbled test statistics), so every quote was taken from a single column of one line and statistics were not relied on beyond the percentages and means quoted. Judgement calls: (1) W praktyce#1.2 marked partly because the recall-only step is the condition the source found ineffective, while the title and W praktyce#2 were marked fully backed because they correspond to the recall-relevant (linking) condition; a reader could reasonably argue W praktyce#1.2 is backed as step 1 of the combined procedure, in which case the status would be PASS. (2) Korzyść i dowody#3.2 treated as a source_claim, not a meta_statement, because it states what the figure does and does not show. (3) Korzyść i dowody#1 was not split into a source_description part and a finding part because both are checked against the same snapshot lines. The Ocena dowodów grade letter was not checked.
